clue.text: Drunken search for one drink after another

indicators.note: someone drunken staggers about, so the letters of the next word reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk goes looking for one drink after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, typically beer after a spirit or the reverse.

clue.text: One who lets out anger settles in a short time

indicators.note: one piece settles in, coming to rest inside the other piece

parts.note: HR is the short form of hour, a time
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A landlord's temper flares and then calms down quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles in' is the container signal. 'One who lets out' sounds like a landlord's role; British usage allows a hirer to be the one renting something out.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a hirer can be the party who rents something out, someone who lets out goods or property.

clue.text: Movements of arms that can give away information

definitions.text: Movements of arms that can give away information

parts.words: Movements of arms that can give away information
parts.note: suggests troop movements betraying secrets, but means a signalling system using arm positions and flags

explanation.definitionFit: Signalling by holding flags or arms in set positions passes messages letter by letter.

clue.text: Chased the Spanish hero off

parts.note: to have chased someone is to have run after them
El Cid is the medieval hero of Spain

explanation.surface: Someone pursued the national hero of Spain until he left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'hero off' (a hero departing) but is the definition, as food that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is off has spoiled, and rancid describes fat or butter that has turned sour.

clue.text: Mischievous child allowed to be present, but not visible

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster is permitted to attend so long as nobody can see them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is there in meaning without being stated openly, present yet unseen.

clue.text: Cause of difficulty in assimilating — in Tbilisi, dieting may be unknown

indicators.note: the letters of the place and the activity may be something else entirely when reworked

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, like x

explanation.surface: In Georgia's capital, people may never have heard of going on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is the anagram signal. The first 'in' is only a link word: including its letters would leave one I and one N too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestibility is the property of food that the body struggles to break down and absorb.

clue.text: Normal love affair for wife's toy boy, for example

parts.note: par is the normal or average level, as in 'up to par'
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: An ordinary fling of the kind a wife might have with a younger man.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover, and a married woman's young boyfriend is one example.

clue.text: Man indigenous in N America, said to be genuinely honest

definitions.meaning: an old, now offensive term for a Native American man
from the dated phrase 'honest ...', an assurance that one is telling the truth

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a fill-in: the word completes the old pledge 'honest ___!' meaning 'truly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dated slur for a Native American and also the second word of an old oath of sincerity.

clue.text: Embarrassed, being queasy when not standing to attention

parts.note: someone queasy feels ill
the military command 'at ease' lets soldiers relax from attention

explanation.surface: A soldier feels sick and awkward once allowed to relax on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel ill at ease is to feel uncomfortable or self-conscious, as when embarrassed.

clue.text: One who can stand listening to music

definitions.text: One who can stand listening to music

parts.words: One who can stand listening to music
parts.note: seems to mean someone who tolerates music, but means a concertgoer who literally stands, as at London's summer Proms

explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a London summer concert series where many in the audience stand in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertgoer at the Proms who buys a cheap standing place in the arena is called by this name.

clue.text: Woman rejecting lover once found in ditch

definitions.meaning: an archaic noun for a woman who casts off a suitor
to ditch a partner is to drop them abruptly

explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is only a link; the old noun sense meant a woman who rejects a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means abandoning a lover, and archaically the noun meant a woman who did so.

clue.text: Fat and perspiring in heat?

definitions.meaning: the fat that runs off roasting meat, used in cooking
sweating heavily on a hot day, soaked through

explanation.definitionFit: The word names cooking fat from a roast and also describes someone streaming with sweat.

clue.text: Detailed record

definitions.meaning: very precise and thorough, as in close attention
the official written record of a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is pronounced differently in its two senses: my-NEWT for detailed, MIN-it for a record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means meticulous, and the noun is a note in the official record of proceedings.

clue.text: A bit neurotic concerning money

indicators.note: only a bit of the word that follows is wanted, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A slightly anxious person worrying about finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency used across much of the European Union.

clue.text: Ragged pauper's C of E (capitals here, please)

indicators.note: ragged suggests tattered and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word is used with its S
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby beggar belongs to the Church of England, and the writer asks for block letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' rearranges PAUPERS with C and E from 'C of E' (Church of England); 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper case is the set of capital letters, where forms often ask you to print.

clue.text: Cooking pot that'll contain neck roast? Yes and no

parts.note: neck is cheek or impudence, which in British slang is also sauce
to roast a show is to criticise it harshly, to pan it

explanation.surface: Will this pot hold a roasted neck of lamb? Well, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' admits the pot holds no meat at all; it is built from words meaning cheek and criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a deep cooking pot with a long handle.

clue.text: Missionary leaving church in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A preacher abandons the church amid difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges LEAVING plus CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic describes zeal for spreading the gospel, the spirit of a missionary.

clue.text: Fortune teller succeeded in becoming a song-writer

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded goes in the fortune teller

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading palms
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant did well enough to turn to writing songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalmist writes psalms, the sacred songs of the Bible.

clue.text: Overcoming resistance, sip sake, involved in social occasion

indicators.note: one piece overcomes, sitting over and around, the other
involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone overcomes their reluctance and sips Japanese rice wine at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is the anagram signal and 'Overcoming' the container signal: the resistance letter sits inside the reworked drink and sipping words.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising that follows a day's skiing at a resort.

clue.text: Wife having left, hesitate to make a statement

indicators.note: the letter for wife has gone away from the word

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate

explanation.surface: After his wife walks out, a man hesitates before saying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' removes W from WAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, to assert something as a fact.

clue.text: A tenor out of touch

parts.note: the tenor of a speech is its general sense or drift

explanation.surface: A singer who has lost contact with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks like a singer but means drift, the gist of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adrift means being lost or detached, out of contact with what is happening.

clue.text: Curb wedding's noise

indicators.note: noise points to the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: to bridle is to curb or restrain

explanation.surface: Stop the racket at the marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noise' signals a word that sounds like BRIDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal means belonging to a bride or wedding, so it can stand for a possessive like wedding's.

clue.text: Made a hole, upsetting maker of jeans

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug a hole or tunnel

explanation.surface: Someone tore a hole and ruined a pair of jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns MINED backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the tough cotton fabric jeans are made of.

clue.text: At home, information in spoken French is poor

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the word for information goes in the French word

parts.note: dit is French for said or spoken
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Information delivered at home in spoken French says that someone is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy or impoverished, a formal word for poor.

clue.text: Relation pernickety about English usage

indicators.note: one word goes about, all round, the abbreviation

parts.note: nice in its older sense means fastidious or finely discriminating

explanation.surface: A relative who fusses about correct English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usage' completes the surface only and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a relation, the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Code name for some grass

parts.note: a legal code is a body of law

explanation.surface: A secret word for a certain kind of cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an area of mown grass.

clue.text: Indicated approving Italian deli, being without a cook

indicators.note: to cook figures is to alter them, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An Italian delicatessen that has no chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from ITALIAN DELI, then 'cook' rearranges what is left; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting one's initials on a document marks approval of it, signing it off.

clue.text: In which one studies figures from all angles

definitions.text: In which one studies figures from all angles

parts.words: In which one studies figures from all angles
parts.note: sounds like viewing a person's shape from every side, but means the study of shapes and their angles

explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with shapes, lines and angles.

clue.text: Watch the tape machine

definitions.meaning: slang for a timepiece, so called for the noise it makes
a telegraph device that printed news or share prices on paper tape

explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for a watch and the name of the machine printing stock prices on tape.
